policies.title: Irish ordinary passports: specified visa-free short visits
policies.summary: Current Irish DFA entry guidance expressly records visa-free ordinary Irish-passport access for the listed destinations.
conditions: VG: no visa is required. CU: no visa is required, but a tourist card and a D’Viajeros arrival form are required; the card is not normalized as a visa.
XK: visit visa-free for up to 90 days. UA: visa-free stays up to 90 days; martial-law, border accessibility, security, dual-nationality and final-admission rules remain separate.
PA: visa-free for up to 90 days. BA: visa-free short visits up to 90 days. TN: no visa is required; the DFA page does not state a duration.
This records visitor baselines only, not work, residence, study, transit, special documents, carrier rules or final admission.

policies.title: Irish ordinary passports: Palestinian-territory access via Israeli ETA-IL
policies.summary: The DFA says visa-exempt Irish citizens passing through Israeli-controlled crossings to Palestine need ETA-IL.
conditions: All entry and exit to Palestine is controlled by Israel. The required ETA-IL applies to travel through Israeli-controlled crossings, rather than constituting a Palestinian visa.

The authorization has its stated validity and multiple-entry limits, but checkpoints, Gaza access, closures, permits, residence, security screening and final admission remain separately controlled and may prevent access.

policies.title: Irish ordinary passports: expressly available visitor visas on arrival
policies.summary: Current Irish DFA guidance expressly describes a border-issued visitor visa route for each listed destination.
conditions: DJ: a tourist visa may be purchased on arrival for cash in USD. KM: a visa is available at Hahaya airport or other points of entry for the stated fee.
KH: a tourist visa is available at the Cambodian border; two passport photographs and USD payment are stated, and the tourist visa is stated as one month with one possible one-month extension.

Cambodia also offers a tourist e-Visa, but the expressly available arrival-issued route is the status recorded for this pair. Final-admission, entry-point, purpose, document and health conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Irish ordinary passports: expressly electronic visitor visas
policies.summary: Current Irish DFA guidance expressly states an electronic visa route for the listed destinations.
conditions: IQ: the DFA states that visas can be obtained online via the Republic of Iraq Ministry of the Interior website. Federal-Iraq and Kurdistan-region rules, entry points, security, purpose and final admission remain separate.
GQ: the DFA expressly says Irish citizens can apply online for an electronic visa. Passport validity, health, purpose, entry-point and final-admission rules remain applicable.

policies.title: Irish ordinary passports: expressly pre-departure mission visas
policies.summary: DFA guidance establishes an advance mission-application or pre-flight possession requirement for these ordinary Irish-passport visitor routes.
conditions: GW: applications are made in person at Guinea-Bissau diplomatic missions in Paris or Lisbon. LR: applications from Ireland are submitted to the Liberian Embassy in London.

SS: the DFA says a visitor cannot fly to Juba without a valid visa, establishing that the visa must be held before departure; the page does not normalize any online filing channel as electronic issuance.
Visitor purpose, document, sponsor, registration, health, security and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

conflicts.explanation: DFA explicitly says Irish citizens do not require a visa. The required tourist card and D’Viajeros form are not an electronically issued visa.
DFA says Irish citizens apply in person at Guinea-Bissau diplomatic missions in Paris or Lisbon, establishing an advance mission route rather than border issuance.
DFA directs applications from Ireland to the Liberian Embassy in London; it does not establish electronic issuance.
DFA says visitors cannot fly to Juba without a valid visa, establishing a pre-departure visa requirement but not electronic issuance.

unresolved.reason: DFA says a visa is required, but does not establish an advance, electronic or arrival issuance route; the Afghan Embassy in London is closed. Generic visa wording cannot be normalized under the strict taxonomy.
DFA says entry is highly restricted and borders remain mostly closed, while the taxonomy has no closed-border or entry-prohibited state. A generic visa-required classification would be misleading.
DFA says a visa is required and refers travellers to the nearest embassy, but does not establish advance, electronic or arrival issuance for an ordinary Irish passport.
DFA says a visa is required and refers travellers to the Sudanese Embassy in London, but does not state issuance timing or establish electronic or arrival issuance.
DFA says only that Irish citizens require a visa. It does not establish whether the current visitor visa is advance-issued, electronic or border-issued.

DFA says Irish citizens require permission and that there is no visa on arrival, but it does not establish the ordinary visitor visa issuance channel. The transit-visa embassy statement is not generalized to visits.
DFA says a visa is required and refers travellers to the Republic of Congo Embassy in London, but does not establish the issuance channel or timing.
DFA says a visa is required and points to Gabon's High Commission, but does not establish an advance, electronic or arrival-issued route.
DFA says a visa is required and points to the Central African Republic Embassy in Paris, but does not establish the issuance channel or timing.
DFA says a visa is required and refers travellers to Côte d’Ivoire's Embassy in the United Kingdom, but does not establish electronic, advance or arrival issuance.
DFA says a visa is required but does not establish an advance, electronic or arrival issuance route.
DFA says a visa is required and refers travellers to Niger's Embassy in Geneva, but does not establish issuance timing or channel.
DFA says a visa is required and links Nigeria Immigration Service, but an online application form does not by itself establish electronic issuance or exclude a mission route.
DFA says a visa is required and refers travellers to the Bangladesh High Commission in London, but does not establish electronic, advance or arrival issuance.
DFA says a visa is required and refers travellers to a Chadian embassy, but does not establish electronic, advance or arrival issuance.
